headline: A stormy, wet week: a stronger Pacific storm Wednesday night into Thanksgiving brings around an inch of rain to the Puget Sound lowlands, possible high winds on the coast and North Interior, and the potential for major coastal flooding along the Strait of Juan de Fuca and Puget Sound shorelines at Thanksgiving's very high tides.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Rain from the first of a series of weather fronts spread inland early Tuesday, but a lull is likely late morning into the afternoon, especially away from the coast, before what is left of the front pushes onshore this evening for another round of rain. Gusty east to southeast winds continue through the day across the Puget Sound lowlands, including around Seattle, and are strongest on the coast, where a Wind Advisory runs until 10 PM Tuesday for the north and Grays Harbor coasts and the western and southern Olympic foothills. A Winter Weather Advisory covers the Cascades of Whatcom and Skagit counties until 10 PM Tuesday.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Any break in the rain and wind Wednesday will be brief as a stronger storm, driven by a powerful jet-stream wind core far offshore, heads in. Strong southeast winds could reach high-wind levels Wednesday night into early Thursday on the coast and across the North Interior, with gusts of roughly 40–50 mph near the coast and northern areas and about 30–40 mph elsewhere, including Seattle, through Thursday. From about 4 PM Wednesday to 4 PM Thursday, rain totals reach around an inch in the interior lowlands outside the Olympic rain shadow (the drier zone around Sequim and Port Angeles should see less), 2+ inches on the coast, 3–5 inches in the Olympics and 1.5–3 inches in the Cascades; snow levels stay well above the passes, though a Winter Storm Watch covers the Whatcom and Skagit Cascades late Wednesday night through Thursday afternoon. A Flood Watch runs Wednesday morning through Sunday afternoon for the Olympics and their western and southern foothills, Olympia and southern Puget Sound, southern Hood Canal, the Chehalis Valley and the Willapa and Black Hills, and the Skokomish River in Mason County will likely flood around midweek, reaching moderate and possibly near-major levels, though no widespread river flooding is expected.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Confidence is only fair for Thursday night through the weekend. High pressure may build into California, but Western Washington sits too far north to benefit much, as storms ride over the top of it into the area, so any weekend break will be brief. Computer models agree that another broad low-pressure pattern settles offshore early next week, bringing a return to more active, wet and windy weather as December arrives.

coast: High surf, low air pressure and some of the year's highest tides create the potential for major coastal flooding, peaking Wednesday on the Pacific coast and on Thanksgiving Day for inland shorelines. A Coastal Flood Warning runs until 3 PM Tuesday for the Eastern and Western Strait of Juan de Fuca (including the Sequim and Port Angeles shore) and the north and Grays Harbor coasts, and until 4 PM for San Juan County; Coastal Flood Advisories run until 5 PM Tuesday for the Seattle, Everett, Island County, Pierce/south King, Skagit/Snohomish and Whatcom lowland shorelines and until 3 PM for the lower Chehalis River valley. Coastal Flood Watches then cover the Strait of Juan de Fuca, Port Townsend, Puget Sound, Kitsap, northern Hood Canal, the San Juans and the outer coast from late Tuesday night through Wednesday afternoon and again from late Wednesday night through Thursday afternoon. A High Surf Advisory covers the north and Grays Harbor coasts until 4 PM Wednesday, with long-period seas of 18–22 feet through Friday, easing to 10–13 feet Friday and 6–8 feet Saturday before building back to 10–13 feet early next week. For boaters, a Storm Warning covers the waters 10–60 miles offshore until 11 PM Tuesday (then a Gale Warning to 4 PM Wednesday), Gale Warnings run through 4 PM Wednesday for the near-shore coastal waters and the east Strait, the west Strait's Gale Warning ends at 4 PM Tuesday and gives way to a Small Craft Advisory until 4 PM Wednesday, and Small Craft Advisories also cover Admiralty Inlet, the northern inland waters and San Juans and the Grays Harbor bar (rough to severe bar conditions) until 4 PM Wednesday and the central Strait until 4 AM Wednesday. Thursday's front brings another round of potentially storm-force winds to the coastal waters and likely gales in the east Strait, possibly in the northern inland waters too, before a reprieve Friday; winds pick up again later in the weekend, affecting small craft on the coastal waters and western Strait.
watch_for: Possible major coastal flooding at high tide along the Strait of Juan de Fuca and Puget Sound shorelines, peaking Thanksgiving Day.
High winds Wednesday night into early Thursday on the coast and in the North Interior.
Heavy rain in the Olympics and river rises, with the Skokomish River likely to reach moderate or near-major flood levels midweek.
confidence: Forecasters are confident in a wet, windy week with the strongest storm Wednesday night into Thursday, have only fair confidence in the details from Thursday night through the weekend, and are more confident in another active stretch starting early next week.
